questions.question: Tokyo Olympian C. A. Bhavani Devi is associated with which sport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fencing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **C. A. Bhavani Devi** is India’s first-ever fencer to qualify for the Olympics.
 
• She represented India in the **Tokyo Olympics 2020** in the women's individual sabre category.
 
• Bhavani Devi made history by **winning her first match against Tunisia’s Nadia Ben Azizi** in the Tokyo Olympics, marking a significant milestone for Indian fencing.
 
• She has won several medals at international fencing competitions, including the **Commonwealth Championship and Asian Championships**.
 
• She was awarded the **Arjuna Award** in 2022 for her remarkable achievements in fencing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shooting**

 
 
• Shooting is a precision-based sport involving firearms like rifles, pistols, and shotguns.
 
• India has produced world-class shooters, including **Abhinav Bindra**, who won India’s first individual Olympic gold medal in the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
 
• The National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) governs the sport in India.
 
• Events like **10m air rifle, 10m air pistol, and trap shooting** are popular categories in international shooting championships.
 
 
 
• **Badminton**
 
 
• Badminton is a racquet sport played using a shuttlecock across a net.
 
• India has excelled in badminton at the international level, with stars like **P. V. Sindhu**, **Saina Nehwal**, and **Kidambi Srikanth** winning medals in Olympics and World Championships.
 
• The Badminton World Federation (BWF) is the governing body for the sport.
 
• It is one of the most popular sports in India, with several domestic and international tournaments held annually.
 
 
 
• **Gymnastics**
 
 
• Gymnastics is a sport involving physical exercises that require strength, flexibility, balance, and coordination.
 
• India's **Dipa Karmakar** made history in gymnastics by becoming the first Indian female gymnast to qualify for the Olympics in 2016.
 
• Artistic, rhythmic, and trampoline gymnastics are the primary categories in international competitions.
 
• The sport is governed globally by the Fédération Internationale de Gymnastique (FIG).

questions.question: Announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, what is the primary objective of the National Geospatial Mission?

options.text: To create and manage an integrated geospatial infrastructure for governance and development
To promote satellite launch services for private companies
To provide free GPS services to rural areas
To monitor climate change patterns through satellite data

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To create and manage an integrated geospatial infrastructure for governance and development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Geospatial Mission** aims to establish an integrated geospatial infrastructure to support governance and development activities across India.
 
• It focuses on ensuring geospatial data availability, accessibility, and usability for various stakeholders, including the government, private sector, and academia.
 
• The mission is designed to align with the vision of **Digital India**, promoting the use of geospatial technologies for decision-making and planning.
 
• It emphasizes the creation of a unified geospatial ecosystem by utilizing advanced technologies like Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, and satellite imagery.
 
• The mission also promotes innovation and entrepreneurship in the geospatial domain, fostering the growth of India’s geospatial industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: To promote satellite launch services for private companies**

 
 
• India has been actively promoting its satellite launch capabilities through organizations like **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation)**.
 
• The **IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center)** was established to encourage private sector participation in space activities, including satellite launches.
 
• However, this is not the primary focus of the National Geospatial Mission, as its objective is related to geospatial data and infrastructure, not satellite launch services.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To provide free GPS services to rural areas**
 
 
• GPS (Global Positioning System) services are already accessible to the public across India, including rural areas, through smartphones and other devices.
 
• While geospatial technologies can enhance rural development, providing free GPS services is not the specific aim of the National Geospatial Mission.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To monitor climate change patterns through satellite data**
 
 
• Satellite data is indeed critical for monitoring climate change patterns, and India has several missions like **INSAT, RISAT, and Cartosat** dedicated to such objectives.
 
• However, the National Geospatial Mission focuses broadly on geospatial infrastructure for governance and development, not exclusively on climate change monitoring.

questions.question: Project _______ is the world's first inter-continental large wild carnivore translocation project.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cheetah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Project Cheetah is the world's first inter-continental large wild carnivore translocation project, initiated in India.
 
• The project aims to reintroduce African cheetahs into India, where the species became extinct in 1952 due to habitat loss and overhunting.
 
• In September 2022, eight African cheetahs were brought to Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh from Namibia under this ambitious conservation program.
 
• The project is part of India's broader wildlife restoration efforts and is executed in collaboration with international organizations and governments, including Namibia and South Africa.
 
• The goal is to establish a viable and secure population of cheetahs in India and restore their ecological role as top predators in the grassland and open forest ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lion**
 
 
• Lions are found in India primarily in the Gir Forest National Park, Gujarat, and are classified as Asiatic lions (Panthera leo persica).
 
• India has undertaken significant conservation efforts under the "Project Lion," focusing on habitat development, reducing human-lion conflict, and increasing their population.
 
• Unlike cheetahs, lions are not part of any inter-continental translocation project.
 
 
 
• **Crocodile**
 
 
• Crocodiles are large aquatic reptiles that inhabit rivers, wetlands, and coastal regions.
 
• In India, species like the mugger crocodile, saltwater crocodile, and gharial are found.
 
• India has conservation programs like the Gharial Conservation Project to protect the critically endangered gharial population.
 
• These efforts focus on breeding and reintroduction within their native ranges rather than inter-continental relocation.
 
 
 
• **Panther**
 
 
• The term "panther" often refers to melanistic leopards or jaguars, which are found in various parts of the world, including India.
 
• Leopards are widely distributed across India and are not subject to inter-continental translocation projects.
 
• Conservation efforts for leopards in India focus on mitigating human-wildlife conflict, habitat conservation, and anti-poaching measures.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Project Cheetah**
 
 
• This project is a significant step in wildlife conservation and biodiversity restoration.
 
• It also aims to raise awareness about the importance of protecting grassland ecosystems, which are often overlooked in conservation efforts.
 
• The initiative highlights India's commitment to global biodiversity goals under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).
 
 
</ul

questions.question: 'Abhanga Vanis' are folk songs of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

• Abhanga Vanis were composed by saints like **Sant Tukaram**, **Sant Namdev**, and other Bhakti movement leaders in Maharashtra.
 
• These songs are a significant part of the **Warkari sect**, which is a spiritual movement dedicated to Lord Vitthal.
 
• The Abhanga tradition is deeply rooted in the Marathi language, reflecting the rich cultural and religious heritage of the state.

• Folk songs in Manipur often depict themes of nature, love, and spirituality and are accompanied by traditional instruments like the Pena.

• Baul singers use simple, heart-touching lyrics and melodies to express their devotion to God and humanity.

• **Tamil Nadu**

questions.question: If a satellite is in the plane of the equator with 0 degrees inclination and at a height of about 36000 km then it is said to be in _______ orbit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geo-stationary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A geo-stationary orbit is a circular orbit located approximately 35,786 km (22,236 miles) above the equator.
 
• In this orbit, the satellite moves at the same rotational speed as Earth, making it appear stationary relative to an observer on Earth.
 
• This type of orbit is ideal for communication satellites, weather observation, and broadcasting purposes.
 
• Geo-stationary satellites have an inclination of 0 degrees, meaning they orbit in the Earth's equatorial plane.
 
• Examples of geo-stationary satellites include INSAT series satellites and weather monitoring systems like GOES.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polar Orbit:**

 
 
• In a polar orbit, the satellite passes over the Earth's poles on each revolution.
 
• These orbits are typically used for Earth observation and remote sensing as they provide global coverage.
 
• Satellites in polar orbits have an inclination close to 90 degrees.
 
• An example of a polar orbit satellite is the NOAA series used for weather forecasting.
 
 
 
• **Elliptical Orbit:**
 
 
• Elliptical orbits are non-circular orbits where the satellite's distance from Earth varies throughout its revolution.
 
• These orbits are used for specific applications such as communication in high-latitude regions (e.g., Molniya orbits).
 
• The satellite spends more time near the apogee (farthest point from Earth), allowing extended coverage over a particular region.
 
 
 
• **Sun-Synchronous Orbit:**
 
 
• Sun-synchronous orbits are designed so that the satellite passes over the same part of the Earth at the same local solar time.
 
• This orbit ensures consistent lighting conditions, making it ideal for imaging and mapping purposes.
 
• These orbits are commonly used by Earth observation satellites like Landsat and Sentinel.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a main factor affecting the rate of evaporation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buoyancy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Buoyancy** refers to the upward force exerted by a fluid on an object submerged in it. It is not a factor affecting the rate of evaporation since evaporation is a surface phenomenon and does not involve the displacement of fluids.
 
• Evaporation is primarily influenced by factors such as surface area, humidity, wind speed, and temperature, while buoyancy is associated with fluid mechanics and does not play a role in this process.
 
• In the context of evaporation, the movement or displacement of the liquid due to buoyancy is irrelevant as evaporation occurs at the liquid's surface.
 
• The rate of evaporation is determined by external environmental conditions, and buoyancy does not alter these factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Surface Area:**
 
 
• The rate of evaporation increases with an increase in the surface area. More molecules are exposed to the air, allowing a higher number of them to escape into the vapor phase.
 
• For example, water in a wide, shallow pan evaporates faster than in a narrow, deep container.
 
 
 
• **Wind Speed:**
 
 
• Higher wind speed increases evaporation by removing the saturated layer of air above the liquid's surface, making room for more molecules to escape.
 
• Wind acts as a dispersing agent, ensuring a lower concentration of water vapor near the surface of the liquid.
 
 
 
• **Humidity:**
 
 
• Humidity refers to the amount of water vapor in the air. High humidity decreases the rate of evaporation as the air is already saturated with water vapor.
 
• Conversely, low humidity accelerates evaporation since the air can accommodate more vapor molecules.
 
 
 
• **General Concept:**
 
 
• Evaporation is the process by which molecules at the surface of a liquid gain enough energy to transition into the gaseous state.
 
• Factors such as temperature, surface area, wind speed, and humidity directly influence the rate of evaporation, while buoyancy is unrelated to this phenomenon.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which railway zone became India's first to switch to compostable bioplastic on trains in August 2025?

• **Northeast Frontier Railway** became India's first railway zone to switch to compostable bioplastic on trains in August 2025, setting an example in sustainable practices.
 
• The initiative aimed to reduce single-use plastic waste by introducing **eco-friendly alternatives** for packaging and disposable items used on trains.
 
• The bioplastics used are **100% compostable**, ensuring they break down naturally and do not harm the environment.
 
• This move is aligned with the Indian government’s policy on **plastic waste management** and its push toward sustainable development goals.
 
• The Northeast Frontier Railway operates in environmentally sensitive areas, including the foothills of the Himalayas, making this initiative vital for regional ecological conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Northern Railway is one of the largest zones in Indian Railways, headquartered in New Delhi.
 
• It is known for operating major train routes like Rajdhani Express and Shatabdi Express.
 
• It has been actively working on implementing green initiatives like solar energy integration at railway stations.

• This zone is recognized for pioneering efforts in electrification and sustainable energy practices.
 
• It has introduced innovative passenger amenities and environmental campaigns but has not yet switched to bioplastics on trains.
 
 
 
• **Western Railway:**

• It has implemented waste segregation and water conservation measures at stations and trains.
 
• Although active in green initiatives, it has not been the first to adopt compostable bioplastic technology.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme:**

• Bioplastics are derived from renewable resources like corn starch and are designed to decompose naturally, unlike traditional plastics.
 
• This initiative aligns with India’s commitment to the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

questions.question: In the context of Microeconomics, the graphical representation of the demand function is called the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**demand curve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The demand curve is a graphical representation of the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity of the good demanded by consumers.
 
• It is typically downward-sloping from left to right, which reflects the law of demand: as the price of a good decreases, the quantity demanded increases, and vice versa.
 
• The demand curve can shift due to factors such as changes in consumer income, tastes and preferences, prices of related goods, or population size.
 
• Each point on the demand curve represents a specific quantity demanded at a corresponding price.
 
• Demand curves are fundamental tools in microeconomics and are used to analyze consumer behavior and market equilibrium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goods Curve:**

 
 
• The term "goods curve" is not a standard concept in economics. It may be confused with the concept of indifference curves or production possibility curves.
 
• Indifference curves represent consumer preferences for two goods, showing combinations of goods that provide the same level of satisfaction.
 
• Production possibility curves represent the trade-off between the production of two different goods, given limited resources.
 
 
 
• **Supply Curve:**
 
 
• The supply curve is a graphical representation of the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity of the good that producers are willing to supply.
 
• It typically slopes upward from left to right, reflecting the law of supply: as the price of a good increases, the quantity supplied also increases, and vice versa.
 
• The supply curve can shift due to factors such as changes in production costs, technology, or government policies.
 
 
 
• **Seller Curve:**
 
 
• "Seller curve" is not a standard term in economics and is not used in the context of microeconomic analysis.
 
• It might be interpreted as referring to the supply curve, which represents the willingness of sellers to provide goods at different price levels.

• **NIP aims to invest Rs. 111 lakh crore in infrastructure projects** by 2025, covering sectors like energy, roads, railways, irrigation, and digital infrastructure.
 
• It includes around 7,400 projects across the country that will be implemented over five years.
 
• The NIP serves as a critical component of India's efforts to achieve the $5 trillion economy goal by 2025.
 
• It ensures better project planning, financing, execution, and monitoring for sustainable infrastructure development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: 2003**
 
 
• In 2003, India was focusing on liberalization and privatization under economic reforms initiated in the 1990s.
 
• While infrastructure development was emphasized, there was no specific initiative like the NIP launched during this year.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: 2008**
 
 
• 2008 was marked by the global financial crisis, which impacted infrastructure investments globally, including in India.
 
• India launched stimulus packages during this period to counter the economic slowdown, but the NIP was not introduced.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: 2013**
 
 
• In 2013, infrastructure projects gained attention under the Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012-2017), focusing on energy, transportation, and urban development.

• The NIP is a visionary project that consolidates infrastructure investments to boost economic efficiency and job creation.

questions.question: Abhijit Sen was the chairman of the Committee on the Wholesale Price Index which submitted its report in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2008**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Abhijit Sen was the chairman of the Committee on the Wholesale Price Index (WPI), which submitted its report in **2008**.
 
• The Committee was constituted to review the existing structure of the WPI and suggest improvements to make it more representative and reflective of the economic realities of the country.
 
• This report formed the basis for revisions in the WPI series, ensuring its alignment with modern economic and industrial developments.
 
• The new WPI series that followed the recommendations of the report used the base year 2004-05, replacing the earlier base year of 1993-94, to reflect updated market realities.
 
• The revised WPI series included new items and removed obsolete ones to better represent the changing consumption and production patterns in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **2004**:

 
 
• This was the base year for the revised WPI series introduced after the Abhijit Sen Committee's recommendations.
 
• It is significant because it reflected updated economic patterns and served as a benchmark for subsequent WPI calculations.
 
• However, the committee itself did not submit its report in 2004 but later in 2008.
 
 
 
• **2006**:
 
 
• In this year, preliminary discussions and reviews regarding the WPI structure were ongoing.
 
• However, the formal submission of the Abhijit Sen Committee report did not occur in 2006.
 
 
 
• **2010**:
 
 
• In 2010, the government introduced a new WPI series with the base year 2004-05, which incorporated the recommendations of the Abhijit Sen Committee submitted earlier in 2008.
 
• However, the committee itself had completed and submitted its work two years prior, in 2008.
 
 
 
• **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)**:
 
 
• The WPI is a measure of the changes in the prices of goods at the wholesale level, reflecting inflation trends in the economy.
 
• It is widely used by policymakers, economists, and businesses to monitor price stability and evaluate inflationary pressures.
 
• The WPI includes three main components: primary articles, fuel & power, and manufactured products.
 
• It plays a key role in decision-making related to monetary policy and economic planning.

questions.question: Which of the following subjects falls under the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Criminal matters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution consists of subjects where both the Centre and State governments can make laws.
 
• Criminal matters are explicitly listed under the Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Entry 1 of the Concurrent List specifically includes "Criminal law" except the procedure for criminal trials, which is covered under a separate entry.
 
• The inclusion of criminal matters in the Concurrent List allows both the Union and State governments to address issues related to criminal laws for maintaining law and order.
 
• In case of any conflict between Union and State laws on Concurrent List subjects, the Union law prevails, as per Article 254 of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Police (Option 1):**

 
 
• The subject of "Police" is included under the State List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution (Entry 2).
 
• States have exclusive legislative and administrative control over police forces within their jurisdiction.
 
• The maintenance of public order through policing is the responsibility of the respective state governments.
 
 
 
• **Radio and television (Option 3):**
 
 
• "Radio and television" fall under the Union List as part of Entry 31.
 
• The Union government has exclusive powers to legislate on matters related to broadcasting and communication technologies.
 
• The Prasar Bharati Act governs public broadcasting services like Doordarshan and All India Radio.
 
 
 
• **Foreign affairs (Option 4):**
 
 
• Foreign affairs are part of the Union List, specifically mentioned under Entry 10 and Entry 11.
 
• The Union government holds exclusive legislative and administrative powers over foreign relations, treaties, and agreements.
 
• This includes matters related to diplomatic missions and international organizations.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List Overview:**
 
 
• The Concurrent List contains 52 subjects, including criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy, and education.
 
• Both the Union and State governments can legislate on these subjects, but Union laws take precedence in case of conflicts.
 
• This list is designed to allow cooperation and shared responsibility between the Centre and States.

questions.question:
In the context of trade policy tools, Which of the following is considered as non-tariff measure?

I. Anti-dumping measures

II. Technical barriers to trade measures
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Non-tariff measures** include restrictions and regulations other than tariffs that affect international trade. Examples include quotas, subsidies, and standards.
 
• **Anti-dumping measures** are non-tariff trade barriers imposed to protect domestic industries from unfair competition caused by imports sold below their normal value.
 
• **Technical barriers to trade (TBT)** refer to regulations, standards, and conformity assessment procedures imposed by countries that may restrict trade.
 
• Both anti-dumping and TBT measures are considered non-tariff measures, as they regulate trade without using direct tariffs.
 
• These measures aim to ensure fair trade practices, protect domestic industries, and maintain quality standards for goods traded internationally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Only I**

 
 
• Anti-dumping measures are specifically designed to counteract dumping, which occurs when foreign producers sell goods in the domestic market at prices lower than their production costs or market value.
 
• However, this option is incorrect because non-tariff measures also encompass technical barriers to trade (Option II).
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Only II**
 
 
• Technical barriers to trade include labeling requirements, health and safety standards, and environmental regulations that may indirectly limit trade.
 
• Although TBT measures are non-tariff measures, this option excludes anti-dumping measures, making it incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Neither I nor II**
 
 
• This option is incorrect because both anti-dumping measures and technical barriers to trade are classified as non-tariff measures.
 
• Non-tariff measures are widely recognized in international trade policy frameworks, including those set by the World Trade Organization (WTO).
 
 
 
• **Option 5: Unavailable**
 
 
• Non-tariff measures, such as anti-dumping and TBT measures, are crucial tools for regulating and ensuring fair trade practices.
 
• These measures allow countries to safeguard their domestic industries and consumers while adhering to international trade agreements.

questions.question: What led to the decline in mortality rate in India during 1921-1951?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Improved health and sanitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Between 1921 and 1951, India witnessed a significant decline in mortality rates primarily due to **advancements in health and sanitation facilities**.
 
• The introduction of modern medical practices, such as vaccinations and antibiotics, contributed to a reduction in deaths caused by infectious diseases like smallpox, cholera, and plague.
 
• Improvements in public health infrastructure, such as better drinking water supply, sewage systems, and cleanliness drives, played a pivotal role in controlling disease outbreaks.
 
• Public awareness campaigns focusing on hygiene and sanitation further improved living conditions, especially in urban areas.
 
• Government initiatives in the health sector during this period, such as the establishment of hospitals and training of medical personnel, laid the foundation for better healthcare access.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second World War**

 
 
• The Second World War (1939–1945) had a devastating impact globally, leading to millions of deaths due to military conflict, famine, and diseases.
 
• In India, the war disrupted food supplies, leading to the Bengal Famine of 1943, which caused significant loss of life.
 
• While the war indirectly led to some technological advancements in medicine, it was not a direct factor in the decline of mortality rates in India during 1921-1951.
 
 
 
• **Increase in birth rate**
 
 
• An increase in the birth rate contributes to population growth but does not directly impact the mortality rate.
 
• During this period, India did experience population growth due to a decline in mortality rates; however, the birth rate itself was not a determining factor in reducing mortality.
 
 
 
• **Artificial Intelligence**
 
 
• Artificial Intelligence (AI) did not exist or play any role in the period between 1921 and 1951.
 
• AI advancements are a modern development that began in the mid-20th century and became prominent in the 21st century.

questions.question: What are the temporary finger-like extensions of the cell surface used by Amoeba to take in food called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pseudopodia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pseudopodia are temporary, finger-like projections of the cell membrane in amoeboid organisms like Amoeba.
 
• They play a crucial role in capturing food particles through a process called phagocytosis.
 
• Pseudopodia are formed by the cytoplasmic streaming mechanism, where the cytoplasm flows into the projections, causing the cell membrane to extend outward.
 
• Besides food intake, pseudopodia also help in locomotion, allowing the Amoeba to move by changing its shape and anchoring itself.
 
• These extensions are highly dynamic structures that continuously change their form to adapt to the environment and facilitate survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flagella:**

 
 
• Flagella are whip-like structures used for locomotion in certain microorganisms such as bacteria and protozoa (e.g., Euglena).
 
• They are made of microtubules and powered by motor proteins that enable the organism to move in liquids.
 
• Unlike pseudopodia, flagella are permanent structures and are not involved in food intake.
 
 
 
• **Cilia:**
 
 
• Cilia are short, hair-like structures that cover the surface of certain cells (e.g., Paramecium).
 
• They beat rhythmically to enable movement and help in creating water currents for capturing food particles.
 
• Cilia are structurally similar to flagella but are smaller and more numerous.
 
 
 
• **Vacuoles:**
 
 
• Vacuoles are membrane-bound organelles found in cells, primarily used for storage and maintaining cellular homeostasis.
 
• In Amoeba, food vacuoles are formed after the pseudopodia engulf food particles, enclosing them for digestion.
 
• Unlike pseudopodia, vacuoles are not directly involved in the process of capturing food; they function after the food is ingested.
 
 
 
• **Amoeba and its feeding mechanism:**
 
 
• Amoeba is a unicellular organism that uses pseudopodia for both movement and feeding.
 
• The process of food intake begins with the formation of pseudopodia that surround and engulf the food particle, forming a food vacuole.
 
• Enzymes inside the vacuole digest the food, and the nutrients are absorbed into the cytoplasm.
 
• The versatility of pseudopodia is essential for Amoeba's survival, as it enables adaptation to diverse environments.

questions.question: What does 'moksha' stand for in the fourfold objective of life according to Vedic philosophy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spiritual freedom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Moksha** in Vedic philosophy stands for liberation or **spiritual freedom** from the cycle of birth and death (Samsara).
 
• It is considered the ultimate goal of human life and is one of the **fourfold objectives (Purusharthas)** of life in Indian philosophy, along with Dharma, Artha, and Kama.
 
• Moksha represents the attainment of **eternal peace and self-realization** by breaking free from material desires and attachments.
 
• The concept of Moksha emphasizes **union with the ultimate reality or Brahman**, transcending the physical and mental realm.
 
• Practices such as meditation, self-discipline, ethical living, and devotion are considered pathways to achieving Moksha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pursuit of desires (Kama):**

 
 
• Kama refers to the fulfillment of desires, including physical, emotional, and material pleasures.
 
• It is one of the Purusharthas and emphasizes enjoying life responsibly while adhering to Dharma (moral duties).
 
• Kama must be balanced and pursued without causing harm to oneself or others.
 
 
 
• **Social status (Dharma):**
 
 
• Dharma signifies moral duties, righteousness, and ethical living.
 
• It is the foundation for maintaining social order and harmony in life.
 
• Following one's Dharma ensures the well-being of both the individual and society.
 
 
 
• **Wealth accumulation (Artha):**
 
 
• Artha refers to the pursuit of wealth and prosperity to sustain oneself and contribute to societal welfare.
 
• It is important to earn wealth ethically and in alignment with Dharma.
 
• Artha supports the fulfillment of desires and enables the pursuit of higher spiritual goals like Moksha.
 
 
 
• **Fourfold objective (Purusharthas):**
 
 
• Vedic philosophy outlines the fourfold objectives of life: Dharma (ethical duty), Artha (wealth), Kama (desires), and Moksha (spiritual freedom).
 
• These objectives provide a holistic framework for leading a balanced and meaningful life.
 
• The ultimate aim is to achieve Moksha while fulfilling the other three objectives responsibly.
